transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Lucas Chen (Redwood SE), Alicia Ruiz (CISO, Northshore), Ben Carter (Infra Lead), Dana Kim (Product)

Summary: Short discovery on data residency requirements and compliance posture; customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key blockers: strict logging restrictions, data residency to EU/US only for certain products, KMS/HSM requirements, SOC2 + financial services controls and audit logs retention.

Topics: data residency, logging redaction, KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO, HIPAA (vendor overlap), on-prem/private deployment feasibility, network connectivity (VPC/peering), SLA and failover, proof-of-concept benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Lucas is our SE, he'll do the technical bits. Alicia, thanks for making time.
[00:08] Alicia: Thanks Maya. Short intro - I'm Alicia, CISO at Northshore. We have Ben on infra and Dana from product. We're evaluating options for hosting LLM-powered customer support assistants but have strict data residency and logging rules.
[00:18] Ben: Yeah, want to understand what data leaves our VPC, what ends up in logs, and how long things are retained.
[00:27] Lucas: Totally. high level, Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployments - private can be VPC-deployed or fully on-prem. For residency, we can pin requests to region and for private you control the network.
[00:40] Dana: When you say "Hosted" - is that multi-region? Where does customer data live?
[00:46] Maya: Hosted runs in our managed regions; we have options in us-east, eu-west, and ap-southeast for some customers. By default logs and telemetry are in those regions and are retained per our policy, but we can discuss contractual restrictions.
[00:56] Alicia: Our requirement: PII must stay within EU for EU customers, and logs that might contain PII cannot be stored centrally - we need options to disable logging or to ensure redaction and local-only logs. Also we must use our KMS for encryption keys.
[01:12] Lucas: Understood. For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools and can opt for customer VPC peering; logs can be routed to your log collector and we can turn off centralized analytics for that instance. With Private, you run the control plane in your VPC and keys never leave your tenant - which meets the KMS requirement.
[01:30] Ben: How does that work with model updates? If we want Redwood-managed model upgrades but private control plane, do you still pull models into our env?
[01:38] Lucas: Typically we push containerized model artifacts to your environment via a signed release. There's a few modes: we can maintain the artifacts and you pull them, or we can provide images and you run them. We can support an air-gapped workflow with an on-prem package.
[01:50] Alicia: And audit logs - we need immutable audit logs for access to the inference outputs and configuration changes for at least seven years. Is that possible?
[01:58] Maya: We have audit logging shipped; retention is configurable as an add-on in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we have standard retention and can add log export to your syslog/S3 with encryption.
[02:10] Dana: A follow-up - do you ever persist prompts or responses in logs for debugging? We can't have user PII persisted.
[02:17] Lucas: We have configurable logging levels. For PII-sensitive workloads we recommend turning off prompt/response logging or enabling automatic PII redaction. We also offer prefix/KV cache options that avoid writing raw prompts to long-term storage.
[02:31] Ben: You said KV cache - is that the same as the KV cash people talk about? (laughs)
[02:34] Lucas: (laughs) KV cache, yes. It's in-memory for performance and can be configured not to spill to disk.
[02:40] Alicia: OK. On encryption: we require CMEK with our KMS (Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS) and HSM-backed keys for production. Can Redwood integrate?
[02:49] Lucas: Yes, we support CMEK integrations for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can bring-your-own-key in some regions; otherwise Dedicated/Private give full KMS control and HSM support. We'll need to scope the KMS connectors for the POC.
[03:02] Maya: Quick note - there's sometimes nuance between our "Private" product and a full air-gapped on-prem. We'll clarify those diagrams after this call.
[03:10] Alicia: Good. Another must-have: we cannot allow raw customer data to be used for model improvement/training. Are you training on customer data?
[03:18] Maya: No. We never use customer prompts or responses to train our models unless you opt-in. We have contractual language to that effect.
[03:24] Dana: Related: do you offer isolated model variants? We may want a quantized smaller model for latency-sensitive flows.
[03:30] Lucas: Yes, Dedicated allows you to run pinned model versions and we have quantization profiles. For private you can run recommended variants too. We'll provide performance profiles per model.
[03:38] Ben: How about network connectivity? We prefer VPC peering or private link. Do you support direct connect / private link to avoid public egress?
[03:46] Lucas: We support VPC peering, private link and customer dedicated interconnects for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has private link in supported regions.
[03:53] Alicia: What about SOC 2 and ISO attestation? We need those for procurement.
[03:58] Maya: We are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO27001 docs. I'll share the reports and our security whitepaper.
[04:05] Alicia: Great. Also will need third-party pen test results and a contact for compliance questions.
[04:10] Maya: I'll include that; Lucas will also send a technical note on the network and KMS integration.
[04:15] Ben: Performance - for our workload we need 100 QPS at 200ms p95 for short responses. Do you have reference latency numbers for Dedicated?
[04:23] Lucas: We do. Typical p95s depend on model and batching; Dedicated with reserved GPUs and tuned kernels hits 150-250ms p95 on smaller models for single-turn. We'll send benchmark numbers and recommend a POC to validate with your prompts.
[04:36] Dana: What does the POC look like? We have a three-week compliance review and then procurement windows.
[04:42] Maya: Typical POC: week 0 prep and scoping, week 1 deploy (Dedicated or Private trial), week 2 run traffic and collect metrics, week 3 review and wrap. We'll need an infra contact - Ben - and compliance contact - Alicia - for acceptance criteria.
[04:56] Alicia: Our acceptance criteria: no cross-region data leakage, KMS integration verified, logs either redacted or stored in our controlled bucket, and an initial penetration scan.
[05:05] Lucas: Sounds good. On logging restrictions, we can provide a configuration snippet to disable prompt logging and route traces to your S3 - we'll send that.
[05:15] Ben: One more - disaster recovery and failover. If your hosted region goes down, do you fail over to another region and does that trigger data residency problems?
[05:24] Maya: Smart routing is configurable. For strict residency, you can disable cross-region failover; otherwise we can fail over within the same geo. We'll document options and default behaviors.
[05:36] Alicia: Any limitations around HIPAA? We have a small covered-entity integration later this year and want vendor HIPAA posture.
[05:44] Lucas: Redwood has HIPAA support for Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted, we have BAAs in some cases - need to check for your exact use-case - we'll include that in the follow-up.
[05:55] Dana: On the commercial side, can you share pricing roughs for hosted vs dedicated vs private? We need to budget for a committed reserved capacity if performance looks good.
[06:04] Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet with committed monthly rates for Dedicated and a per-token hosted price. We can model a blended unit cost for your expected traffic.
[06:12] Alicia: Procurement will want contractual language about data residency and penalties for breach - do you accept custom clauses?
[06:18] Maya: We do enterprise addenda and have standard clauses we can iterate on. For strict financial controls we often include SAML SSO, RBAC and audit log requirements in the addendum.
[06:28] Ben: Curious about telemetry - do you collect PII in traces or telemetry?
[06:33] Lucas: Telemetry is aggregated by default; we avoid collecting raw PII in telemetry. For Dedicated/Private we can route telemetry to your collector and limit retention.
[06:42] Alicia: We will also need to know which subprocesses have access to keys and logs - requirement for least privilege and separation of duties.
[06:49] Lucas: We'll provide an access matrix for the deployment: who in Redwood has access, what roles exist, and how RBAC maps to actions. For Private, you control most access.
[06:58] Dana: If we go Private initially for EU data residency and Dedicated for global, is seamless routing supported between the two?
[07:06] Lucas: You can configure routing policies. For production you'd probably route EU traffic to Private and other traffic to Dedicated; we can do automated fallback with guardrails but it's customizable.
[07:16] Alicia: Anything about logging restrictions for regulators? In some cases the regulator asked for redacted logs but with ability to reconstitute if subpoenaed - can you support that?
[07:26] Lucas: We can support pseudonymization with reversible tokenization stored in your KMS so reconstitution is possible under strict controls. We'll add details to the follow-up.
[07:36] Maya: Let's recap next steps - I'll send SOC2, ISO, pen test summary, and pricing. Lucas will send the KMS integration note, private deployment diagram, and logging config snippets. Alicia will send your regulatory checklist and list of must-have contract language. Ben will be our infra contact for the POC.
[07:53] Alicia: Sounds good. A couple minor transcription notes - apologies if some product names were off, I might have said "Redwood Privet" earlier.
[07:59] (laughter)
[08:01] Maya: No worries. We'll follow up in email to lock dates.
[08:05] Ben: Quick question - for the POC, any estimate on infra we need to provision? GPUs, network?
[08:12] Lucas: For initial POC with smaller models, a single A100-equivalent instance with 2-4 reserved GPUs should be fine depending on QPS. We'll send a sizing guide.
[08:23] Dana: One other compliance item - we use strict data retention policies, can you support auto-delete of logs and model traces after X days?
[08:31] Lucas: Yes, retention policies are configurable; automatic deletion hooks to S3 lifecycle or log retention are supported.
[08:38] Alicia: Great, thanks. Any closing notes?
[08:41] Maya: Thanks all. We'll email the artifacts by tomorrow for Maya to send SOC docs and pricing. Lucas will follow up with technical artifacts mid-week.
[08:50] Alicia: Thanks.

End of transcript.

References shared during call: Security whitepaper (link provided post-call), SOC2 report (to be attached), private deployment diagram (to be shared), pricing sheet (to be shared).
